subject: physics
question_text: A body freely falling from a certain height h, after striking a smooth floor, rebounds and rises to a height h/2. What is the coefficient of restitution between the floor and the body?

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 6 VERY SHORT ANSWER (numerical). The 1+1 split — formula, then value — is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher. The arithmetic is hand-checked; no exam appearance years are printed, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

where h₁ is the drop and h₂ the rebound.
steps.margin_note: Name which height is which. The ratio is upside down if you swap them.
steps.why: The speeds before and after go as √h for a free fall, so the ratio of speeds — which is what e means — becomes the square root of the ratio of heights.
common_mistakes: Writing e = h₂/h₁ without the square root.

recall.must_convey: That e = √(h₂/h₁), the rebound height over the drop height.
accept: e equals root of h two by h one
square root of rebound height by drop height

steps.memory_tip: For a floor bounce, e = √(h₂/h₁) — heights, because speed goes as √h in free fall.

steps.why: The answer does not depend on the height you drop it from, only on the pair of surfaces. That is what makes e a useful number.
common_mistakes: Giving e = 0.5 by taking the height ratio instead of its square root.

steps.memory_tip: h₂ = h/2 gives e = 1/√2. Notice the drop height cancels out of e.

insider_note: Two marks, and the first is for e = √(h₂/h₁) alone. An answer that shows only 0.707 collects one of them.
